summary: The Ernst Mach Grant - Worldwide is paid by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research and run by the OeAD. It supports research stays of 1 to 9 months in Austria for doctoral students, postgraduates and post-docs from universities outside Austria, in all disciplines and from all countries except Austria. The grant is a monthly payment towards living costs and does not pay for a degree programme in Austria. Applicants must be no older than 35 when the stay starts and need a supervision confirmation from an Austrian university lecturer.
eligibility_notes:
Open to young researchers of any nationality except Austrian, in all disciplines. Three groups can apply: (a) doctoral/PhD students studying at a university outside Austria; (b) postgraduates and post-docs who want to do research in Austria for an academic career and who finished their studies at a non-Austrian university after 30 September 2025; (c) post-docs who work as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria.

Age: no older than 35 when the research stay starts.

Not eligible: current students of an Austrian university, people permanently resident in Austria, and people whose education was mainly in Austria. Someone already in Austria as a visiting scholar cannot apply for the current stay; they may apply for a later stay only if they have not lived, studied, researched or worked academically in Austria in the six months before the grant begins.

The grant does not pay for a full or partial PhD, master's or other degree programme in Austria. It is for short research or study stays only. No enrolment is needed.

The applicant needs a written confirmation of supervision from a lecturer at an Austrian university. OeAD does not help find one; applicants search the websites of Austrian universities and contact professors themselves. The supervisor may not also write the recommendation letter (such a letter is invalid). The supervisor must confirm the project can be carried out in English.

Language: no official test such as TOEFL is required, but the applicant needs enough English for the subject.

Stays must fall in the 2027/28 Austrian academic year; the earliest start is September 2027 and extensions are not possible. Stays must be planned in full calendar months, starting on the first and ending on the last day of a month.

Generative AI may be used for the application but any use must be declared, with the tools used and to what extent.
age_experience_notes: Maximum age 35 when the research stay starts (OeAD page and FAQ). The OeAD's general guideline for incoming scholarships lists an age limit of 45 for scientists with a doctorate in some programmes; for the worldwide grant the current page and FAQ give 35. No minimum work experience is stated.
funding_summary: A monthly grant for a stay of 1 to 9 months, paid by OeAD. The OeAD pages do not give the monthly rate for this call. The ministry's general guideline sets a ceiling of EUR 2,800 per month for incoming scholarships, with the actual rates fixed each year by ministry decree, and says the grant is set on the assumption that real living costs in Austria are higher than the grant. A travel subsidy of up to EUR 2,000 exists for citizens of listed developing countries. OeAD states the grant may not cover all costs, own funds are needed, and the rate cannot be increased, for example for family members.
programmes_note: All disciplines are eligible. The grant funds a research or study stay of 1 to 9 months, not a degree programme. The research plan is described in the online form (no separate proposal upload), meeting the minimum word counts in the form. Applications must cover full calendar months. For short stays of 1 to 3 months OeAD suggests January to June because accommodation can be hard to find otherwise.
institutions_note: All Austrian universities can host grantees. Non-university research institutes are assessed case by case by OeAD before applying; the supervisor must work at that institute and also teach at a university. The applicant finds the host and supervisor; OeAD does not arrange this.

summary.detail: Doctoral/PhD students studying at a university outside Austria can spend 1 to 9 months doing research in Austria under an Austrian university supervisor. All disciplines. Maximum age 35 at the start of the stay. Proof of the doctoral study at the home university is required. The grant does not fund a doctorate in Austria.

Post-docs and other postgraduates who finished studies at a non-Austrian university after 30 September 2025 and aim for an academic career, and post-docs who lecture or research at a university outside Austria, can spend 1 to 9 months doing research in Austria. All disciplines. Maximum age 35 at the start of the stay. Proof of employment at the home university is required for scientists.
summary.source_text: post-docs working as lecturers or researchers

benefits.limit_text: Monthly grant for 1 to 9 months; the monthly rate is not stated on the OeAD pages read. The ministry guideline gives a ceiling of up to EUR 2,800 per month for incoming scholarships, with actual rates set each year
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly by OeAD by cheque or to an account in the euro area. Permanent presence at the place of study or research in Austria is required. The grant is a contribution to costs, not full cover; own funds are needed and the rate cannot be raised for family members. It is reduced if other grants or income above the small-earnings limit are received (employment kept with the home institution is not counted). No paid work is allowed apart from minor academic or artistic work at universities and research bodies.

benefits.limit_text: Travel subsidy of up to EUR 2,000 for citizens of, and travelling from, listed developing countries (OECD DAC list: least developed, low income and lower middle income countries, plus Gabon, Malaysia, Namibia, South Africa and Thailand)
benefits.conditions: Claimed by sending a settlement with original receipts without being asked; OeAD spot-checks the receipts. Applicants from other countries pay their own travel. Whether the subsidy is paid for this call is taken from the general ministry guideline, not from the 2027/28 FAQ.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation is the grantee's own cost
benefits.conditions: The FAQ lists accommodation and deposits as extra expenses. OeAD sends information on housing options with the award contract.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance is the grantee's own cost
benefits.conditions: The FAQ lists health insurance among extra expenses; the residence authority may require proof of insurance and funds. OeAD gives information on accident and health insurance with the award contract.

benefits.limit_text: Visa and residence permit costs are the grantee's own
benefits.conditions: OeAD does not require proof of funds itself, but the Austrian residence authority may (for example when accommodation costs more than EUR 386.43 per month in 2026).

requirements.text: Online application form completed in the OeAD application system, including personal data, academic education, the planned research stay and a financing plan; the research plan is written in the form (no separate proposal file) and must meet the minimum word counts
Valid biometric passport (a national ID card is accepted only from EU applicants)

Confirmation of supervision from a lecturer at an Austrian university, on the OeAD template, with date, signature and stamp, not older than six months. The supervisor may not also write a recommendation letter.

Recommendation letters (freely worded) with letterhead, date, signature and university or department stamp, not older than six months; normally uploaded to the applicant's online account, or sent as scans by the referee before the deadline
Proof of degrees already obtained, copies of originals
Written proof of doctoral studies at the home university
Written proof of employment at the home university
requirements.conditional_rule: Post-docs and other scientists employed at a university outside Austria

requirements.text: Declaration of any use of generative AI tools in preparing the application (which tools and to what extent)
Documents not in English or German: upload a copy of the original plus an English or German translation (a rough translation is enough; certified translation not required)

application_steps.title: Find an Austrian supervisor and plan full calendar months
application_steps.detail: Look for an institute and professor at an Austrian university and obtain a written supervision confirmation on the OeAD template; OeAD cannot help find one. Plan a stay of 1 to 9 months in the 2027/28 academic year, starting no earlier than September 2027, from the first to the last day of whole months. Non-EU applicants planning more than six months should allow for slow residence permit processing.

application_steps.title: Prepare letters, passport and proof of status
application_steps.detail: Get recommendation letters with letterhead, date, signature and stamp (not older than six months; not from the supervisor), a valid biometric passport, proof of degrees, and proof of doctoral study or employment. Documents in other languages need the original plus an English or German translation. Only genuine wet-ink or certified digital signatures are accepted.

application_steps.title: Submit the online application by 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
application_steps.detail: Fill in the online form, describing the planned research thoroughly and meeting the minimum word counts, declare any AI use, and upload the documents. Late documents are not accepted and an incomplete application can be rejected as formally invalid. OeAD advises not to wait until the last minute because the submission check takes time and technical support is closed outside office hours.

application_steps.title: OeAD checks that the application is formally valid
application_steps.detail: OeAD first checks the formal criteria. Applications with missing information, an insufficiently described research stay or too few characters are rejected as formally invalid, even when all documents are uploaded. A faulty application cannot be corrected, but a better one may be sent at the next call.

application_steps.title: Subject experts evaluate and a committee awards
application_steps.detail: Formally valid applications go to subject experts. According to the ministry guideline the reviewers look at why you want to work in Austria, what exactly you will do, the methods and steps, the research aim, earlier preparatory work, where you will work, and your study record or publication list. Stays of 1 to 3 months are reviewed by the named supervisor; stays of 4 months or more by the supervisor and an external expert. A selection committee awards the best applicants, and the ministry decides within available funds.

application_steps.title: Results are expected at the beginning of July 2027
application_steps.detail: All applicants are told the outcome. The applicant and the Austrian supervisor are informed by email.

application_steps.title: Accept the award and sort out entry to Austria
application_steps.detail: Successful applicants receive a Letter of Award with the next steps; the guideline says OeAD then sends a written offer that must be accepted in writing within a set period, and sends information on insurance, housing, residence law and admission. Non-EU nationals with stays over six months should contact their embassy right away to start the visa process, which can take several months; a July award can make a September start unrealistic.

application_steps.title: Stay in Austria and report on progress
application_steps.detail: Permanent presence at the research place in Austria is required. At the end of each semester a written report countersigned by the supervisor shows whether the planned project is being carried out, and a countersigned final report is due at the end; further payments and the last instalment depend on these reports. Problems must be reported at once to OeAD. No paid work is allowed apart from minor academic work, and grantees must help with evaluation of the programme.
